sourceBlog.title: Korea, Japan & Taiwan Digital Nomad Visas

introSlide.heading: 3 Asian digital nomad visas. One clear winner for you.
introSlide.description: Korea, Japan, Taiwan. Same region, very different rules.

slides.heading: How long can you stay?
slides.description: Korea 2 yr | Japan 6 mo hard cap | Taiwan 1–3 yr, renewable indefinitely.

slides.heading: Income requirement
slides.description: Korea ~$64K/yr | Japan ~$68K/yr | Taiwan: qualify in 1 of 12 fields, income varies.

slides.heading: Tax reality
slides.description: Korea 6–45% worldwide after 183 days. Japan 0% foreign income on DN visa. Taiwan 50% exemption on salary above NT$3M.

slides.heading: ARC & housing
slides.description: Korea: full ARC. Japan: no Residence Card, guarantor needed. Taiwan: full ARC.

slides.heading: Path to PR
slides.description: Korea 5+ years. Japan 10+ years. Taiwan 3 years. Taiwan wins by a wide margin.

slides.heading: Best for
slides.description: Korea: 1–2 yr, simple process. Japan: 6 mo test drive, clean tax. Taiwan: high earner, long-term, PR track.

caption:
Korea, Japan, or Taiwan: the right digital nomad visa depends on what you're optimizing for.

For most remote workers who want a simple, livable base: Korea's F-1-D is the easiest entry point. Full ARC, two-year stay, city that works. Catch: after 183 days you're in the Korean tax system on worldwide income (6–45%).

For high earners who want tax efficiency: Japan's Digital Nomad visa gives you 6 months as a non-resident, 0% Japanese tax on foreign income. No Residence Card means housing is harder, but it's the cleanest short-term tax position in East Asia.

For long-term settlers: Taiwan's Gold Card gives 1–3 year stays, full ARC, and PR in just 3 years. Strongest long-term package if you qualify in one of 12 fields.
